dataset_or_source: UHOP Schedule E-1 and RHOP Schedule D land-use designations
finding: No public machine-readable layer exists for Hamilton's citywide Official Plan land-use designations (UHOP Schedule E-1 urban and RHOP Schedule D rural). The City's plan pages offer PDFs only.
evidence: Live ?f=json and /query checks 2026-10-17 | all 1,697 layers on spatialsolutions.hamilton.ca/webgis/rest/services | all 594 services in Hamilton's ArcGIS Online org (covers open.hamilton.ca) | McMaster | Mohawk | UWaterloo | Hamilton Conservation Authority | Ontario GeoHub: none carry E-1 or D designations | Schedule E is Urban Structure and the designations are on E-1
implication: Citywide designation is a named gap. Fill by requesting the internal layer from the City (authoritative) or by vector extraction from the schedule PDFs (see PI-0007). Use secondary plan land use (PI-0002) and Employment Lands (PI-0004) meanwhile.

finding: Layer is cut to individual lots (median about 814 m2) so polygons need dissolving by plan and class. Four retired plans are still present and must be filtered. implication: Dissolve and filter retired plans in normalize. Build a plan-name crosswalk to the boundary layer. Record licence as not stated (licences are not a gate, Morgen 2026-10-17).

finding: Employment Lands layer has 22 polygons grouped by named employment district. The City says they are based on the Schedule E-1 employment designations, but they are not drawn per designation.

evidence: Viewer app configs reference itvpgisappint.hamilton.ca | no public DNS resolution (checked 2026-10-17)
implication: Do not retry from outside (HARD-RULES 9). The only route is a request to the City for the internal designation layer.

finding: A search hit that looked like a Hamilton 2019 Official Plan Schedule E layer belongs to Thunder Bay, not Hamilton.
evidence: https://services5.arcgis.com/h9xShea49ZANgOtx/ArcGIS/rest/services/OP2019_CommercialLandUseDesignations/FeatureServer (checked 2026-10-17)

implication: Viable fallback for the PI-0001 gap. See effort estimate PI-0008.

dataset_or_source: NPCA assessment parcels vs City of Hamilton parcels
finding: NPCA and Hamilton city parcels show a constant offset of about 0.98 m (Hamilton about 0.30 m east and 0.94 m south of NPCA), likely a datum difference. Shifting by that vector gives 100% overlap.
evidence: Grok Bot comparison of NPCA and City of Hamilton parcel layers clipped to Hamilton (local-data only)
implication: Apply or account for the shift before spatial joins between NPCA-derived and City parcels. Centre-point joins tolerate it for now.

finding: First Hamilton view should load framed by the Greenbelt and all conservation/natural layers so the city appears encased by nature.
evidence: Morgen direction in chat 2026-10-17 (focus/hamilton/INSIGHTS.md)
implication: Front-end first-view layer stack for Hamilton includes Greenbelt, NEP and conservation authority layers by default.

finding: Full-population check confirms the NPCA offset: 90102 reciprocal pairs give dx +0.297 m and dy -0.939 m (City minus NPCA), IQR under 3 mm. After the shift IoU p50 is 1.000 and 89837 of 90102 pairs reach IoU 0.9, up from 25402.
evidence: Spine check on all 90306 NPCA and 166828 City parcels in EPSG:26917 2026-10-17 | heavymap-planning/focus/hamilton/SPINE-BASE-PULL-2026-10-17.md
implication: The two fabrics are the same parcels. Shift NPCA before every join. Confirms PI-0010 on the full population.

finding: NPCA stores its own UTM centroids as attributes. Those stored centroids sit +0.30 m east and -0.93 m north of NPCA served geometry, which matches the City fabric. The offset is therefore introduced in NPCA hosted geometry, not in the City layer. Parcels_Cityview shows the identical offset.
evidence: 3000-row sample (seed 42) of CentroidX/CentroidY vs geometry centroid | Cityview 4966/5000 reciprocal sample with dx 0.297 dy -0.939 (2026-10-17)
implication: Treat the City fabric as the reference geometry and correct NPCA-hosted layers. Probably a datum transformation at publish time on NPCA side.

finding: First spine check: 90102 of 90306 NPCA parcels (99.77%) are reciprocal 1:1 with City parcels after the shift. 90162 City parcels get an ARN. Only 13 NPCA and 31 City parcels in the overlap are unmatched. 189 NPCA parcels each cover several City parcels (2538 City parcels) and 101 City parcels hold more than one ARN.
evidence: spine-check.json and join-checks.json on deb local-data/hamilton-city/_profile-2026-10-17 | heavymap-planning/focus/hamilton/SPINE-BASE-PULL-2026-10-17.md
implication: ARN can be attached to about 54% of Hamilton parcels now (NPCA watershed only). The rest of the city needs another roll-number source.

dataset_or_source: Hamilton Addresses, Buildings and Waste Collection by Address
finding: Addresses join cleanly to parcels: 273509 of 274725 points fall in exactly one parcel. Buildings: 213676 of 214292 rep points in exactly one parcel. Waste Collection by Address matches Addresses on 271875 of 277701 rows including unit.
evidence: join-checks.json 2026-10-17 | heavymap-planning/focus/hamilton/SPINE-BASE-PULL-2026-10-17.md
implication: Point-in-polygon is enough for address and building attachment. Waste collection is a free second address register to cross-check units.

finding: None of the City base layers publish a stable ID. Parcels, addresses and buildings carry only OBJECTID (service row id). The parcel layer has no attributes at all beyond area and length.
evidence: Layer metadata ?f=json 2026-10-17 for Hamilton_Assessment_Parcel/0, Addresses/1, Buildings/8
implication: The HeavyMap ID registry must mint parcel, address and building IDs. Matching uses geometry fingerprint plus ARN and address key as aids.

finding: NPCA civic address (STREET_NUM + FULL_STREE) equals a City address point on the same parcel for 84387 of 88167 tested parcels (95.7%) by plain upper-case match. 4051 matched NPCA parcels have no address.
evidence: join-checks.json 2026-10-17
implication: Address agreement is a strong second check on the ARN attachment. Normalising directions and suffixes should lift it further.

finding: All 11 new layers (about 1.0M features, about 510 MB GeoJSON) pulled from the City AGOL org, LIO and the NPCA org in under 6 minutes with no retries, using objectIds batches of 2000. Profiling, the full spine check and the join checks each run in under 2 minutes on deb with shapely 2 STRtree.
evidence: pull_hamilton_base.log and script timings on deb 2026-10-17
implication: A whole jurisdiction base pull and spine check is a sub-hour job. The bottleneck is review, not compute.

dataset_or_source: Surface Water Quality Program and MPAC land parcels (catalog Tier 1)
finding: Two of the four Tier 1 key-join rows do not join to parcels. Surface Water Quality is a 3172-row sample table keyed by 68 station codes with no geometry. The MPAC row (C250) is fee-based with no endpoint, so nothing was pulled.
evidence: Surface_Water_Quality_Program/FeatureServer/14 ?f=json 2026-10-17 | hamilton-dataset-groupings.csv C250

finding: The 23 managed-forest rows carry hyphenated roll numbers. 19 start 2518 (Hamilton) and only 8 match an NPCA ARN, because most HCA forests lie outside NPCA coverage.
evidence: ROLL_NUMBER profile and match 2026-10-17
implication: Roll-number registers outside the NPCA area need a roll source for north and west Hamilton before they can attach.

finding: Hamilton {local} is minted as a 26-character Crockford ULID inside hm:ca:on:hamilton:{grain}:{ULID}. Geometry fingerprint and ARN stay matching aids and are never the ID. Stacked duplicate City geometries share one ID with OBJECTID aliases.
evidence: ADR 0003 | tests/test_heavymap_ids.py (16 tests) | Q-001 Q-002 | heavymap-planning/focus/hamilton/DECISIONS.md identity 2026-10-17
implication: Owner review of ADR 0003. Do not reconstruct a Hamilton spine key from ARN, OBJECTID or a content hash of geometry.

finding: The NPCA shift is a per-source config (dx +0.297 m, dy -0.939 m in EPSG:26917) applied before representative-point matching. Registry ARN grades are exact_1to1, one_to_many, many_to_one, unmatched and not_in_coverage. They are not the NA-86 exact/good/weak/refused scale.
evidence: Q-004 | PI-0012 | NA-276 | heavymap/ids/config.py | tests OffsetCorrectionTests and GradeTests
implication: Keep the City fabric as reference geometry. Mapping registry grades onto NA-86 waits for that issue.

finding: This cloud VM could not reach services.arcgis.com (SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, HTTP 000). The environment egress allowlist is GitHub and PyPI only, so no live Hamilton layer pull or full-population registry stats were produced here.

finding: The CLI refuses GeoJSON that looks like lon/lat (bbox in degree space, extent at most 5 degrees). The NPCA translation is in metres. Applying it to EPSG:4326 would mint unstable IDs.
evidence: tests/test_heavymap_ids.py test_lonlat_input_is_refused | pull scripts on deb store 4326 and analyse in 26917
implication: Reproject pulls to EPSG:26917 before minting. The registry does not silently treat degrees as metres.
